b: The company demonstrated its latest technologies, including CeraGrout and drop-lock installation, while introducing an AI agent at the US flooring event.
Wood flooring is one of the applications served by i4F’s flooring technologies (Image: Unsplash)

i4F, a group of companies providing patents and technologies for the flooring industry, showcased its latest innovations at the 2026 Synergy Convention and Expo in the US. Its programme included a private reception, a live demonstration of CeraGrout for floors and walls, and an interactive booth where installers can test its technologies.

Matthieu Dekens, president of i4F, and Nicholas Wodtke, commercial manager for the US, attended the event alongside the company’s new AI agent. Trained on i4F’s technologies and product information, the agent can answer questions in real time and continue learning through interactions. Attendees were able to engage with it at both the private reception and exhibition booth.

Organised by Certified Flooring Installers (CFI) in partnership with FCICA (The Flooring Contractors Association) and FCITS (Flooring Consultants and Inspection Training), the 2026 Synergy Convention and Expo took place from 10–12 Nov at the Chattanooga Convention Centre in Tennessee. The event brought together flooring installers, contractors, inspectors, manufacturers, distributors and other industry professionals.

i4F’s programme began with a private reception on the evening before the convention opened. Attendees had the opportunity to preview the company’s latest technologies and provide feedback directly to its team.

During the convention, i4F presented a live demonstration of its CeraGrout technology for floors and walls. Designed to replicate the appearance of modern ceramic tiles with integrated grout, the product is water-resistant, durable and stain-resistant. It is also designed to offer faster installation than traditional ceramic tiles.

At the Flooring Expo, visitors to i4F’s booth were able to meet the team and explore its technologies. An installation box beside the booth allowed attendees to try out the company’s drop-lock installation system.
“Synergy is all about bringing the flooring installation community together, making it the perfect environment for us to share new ideas and, importantly, hear directly from installers,” said Dekens.

“Our partnership with CFI reflects that same commitment to education and hands-on experience. We want installers to work with our technologies, put them to the test and tell us what they think,” he added. “Our AI agent takes that dialogue a step further. It makes our knowledge available whenever installers need it, and every question it answers helps us understand what matters most to them.”
